title: Hotfix: guard against quantization profile cache stampede (rate-limit + jittered backoff)
author: Noah Patel
description: Context: During the staged rollout of quantization profile resolution we hit a thundering-herd scenario when many workers noticed an expired/invalidated profile entry at the same time. Each worker independently attempted to refresh the artifact from model-registry, leading to a burst of registry QPS + elevated tail latency in the request path; in one region this coincided with 5xx spikes for routes pinned to affected model variants. This PR adds a hotfix guard to prevent profile refresh stampedes by introducing (1) per-process singleflight locking keyed by (model_id, profile_id, hw_scope) so only one refresh is in-flight per key, (2) a token-bucket rate limiter for refresh attempts to cap registry QPS under load, and (3) jittered exponential backoff on refresh failures/timeouts so retry bursts don’t align across workers. Behavior changes: - If a refresh is already in-flight for a key, other workers will wait up to refresh_wait_timeout_ms (default 250ms) for completion, then fall back to stale-but-valid cache if available. - If cache is stale and no valid entry exists, requests fall back to baseline execution path (existing behavior) while refresh continues asynchronously subject to rate limits. - Metrics: added counters + timers for singleflight contention, refresh rate limiting, and backoff events. Safety: This is a hotfix targeted at reducing blast radius; it does not change profile selection logic, compatibility checks, or route policy evaluation. Related: incident notes in #incidents thread-1731349088; original cache fetch work in PR #28766; fallback logic in PR #28805. Testing: unit tests for limiter/backoff behavior; integration test that simulates 128 concurrent refreshers; manual canary in staging with forced registry 429s to validate backoff + baseline fallback.
commits: runtime(cache): add singleflight guard for profile refreshes
runtime(cache): token-bucket limiter for registry fetches + config defaults
runtime(cache): jittered exponential backoff on refresh failures
tests: concurrency + backoff unit tests; integration test harness
review_conversation: Mateo Alvarez: Thanks for jumping on this. Can you clarify what happens if we’re stale and the refresh_wait times out? I want to make sure we don’t block the request path too long.

Noah Patel (author): Yep — wait is bounded by refresh_wait_timeout_ms (250ms default). If it times out and we have a stale-but-valid entry (within max_stale_ms) we serve it; otherwise we fall back to baseline path and let the refresh continue in background (subject to limiter/backoff).
Sean Gallagher: Please add a metric for “waiters timed out” so we can alert on prolonged contention, and ensure defaults are conservative for Private deployments (registry latency can be higher).

Noah Patel (author): Added cache_stampede_wait_timeout_total and made max_stale_ms + refresh_wait_timeout_ms configurable with sane defaults; also documented recommended overrides for Private in runtime_defaults.yaml comments.
Hiro Tanaka: Any risk that backoff delays a legitimate version update too long? For example after publish we want the new profile to land quickly.

Noah Patel (author): Backoff only applies on refresh failure paths (timeouts/429/5xx). On success we refresh immediately; on invalidation events we still attempt refresh right away but limiter caps QPS and other workers singleflight behind the leader.
Logan Wright: Can we tag the new metrics with profile_id + model_id? We need to segment by profile for dashboards but avoid high cardinality if profile ids are too granular.

Noah Patel (author): Added tags: model_family + quant_profile_name (stable) and hw_scope; excluded full profile UUID to avoid cardinality blowups. Also included a debug log line with full key under trace sampling.
Mateo Alvarez: One more ask: please ensure the limiter is per-process (not global) and the keyspace includes hw scope so A100/H100 don’t block each other.
Noah Patel (author): Confirmed: limiter is per-process; singleflight key includes model_id + profile_id + hw_scope + runtime_abi. Added test coverage for hw_scope keying.
Sean Gallagher: Approving for hotfix. Please coordinate canary with Rafael/eng-sre and ensure we have a rollback toggle ready if anything unexpected happens.
Noah Patel (author): Coordinated with Rafael; plan is 5% canary in us-east for 30 min, then 25% and roll forward. Rollback is just reverting runtime image; no config migration required.
release_notes: Hotfix (runtime): prevent quantization profile cache stampedes by adding singleflight refresh, refresh QPS limiting, and jittered backoff; improves stability under invalidation events and registry degradation.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; cherry-picked into release/2026.01.19-hotfix for rapid rollout.
